turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung reassured O-lan, telling her that the eldest son would be well taken care of and that he would ensure all her wishes were fulfilled, even if it meant seeing to the feast with his own hands.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was worried that her eldest son and his wife would not be able to manage without her, and she asked Wang Lung if he had talked to their son about the importance of looking after his new family and respecting his ancestors.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded reassuringly, telling O-lan that he had spoken to their son and that the young man understood his duties and would respect his ancestors.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan let out a sigh of relief, telling Wang Lung that she was glad to hear their son understood his duties. She hoped he would remember her words and take care of his new family with the same devotion she had shown.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He nodded hesitantly, his eyes filled with worry as he looked at his mother. He promised her quietly that he would take care of his new family and never forget her teachings.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid stepped forward quietly, her eyes on O-lan, and offered to help with any preparations for the feast, ensuring everything would go smoothly.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan thanked the maid for her offer, her voice soft but firm, and she hoped the feast would be a joyous occasion for all.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: She assured O-lan that she would see to every detail, from the food to the seating arrangements, to ensure the feast was a celebration as O-lan hoped.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan let out a weary but contented sigh, her gaze softening as she looked at her husband and son. She hoped that her family would find happiness and strength in each other after she was gone.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He nodded again, his voice barely above a whisper as he assured O-lan and Wang Lung that he would do everything in his power to make sure their wishes were fulfilled.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung placed a reassuring hand on O-lan's shoulder, his voice soft but steady as he told her that he would see to everything and make sure their son's marriage would take place as she wished, no matter what.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan nodded, her eyes welling up with tears, and whispered that she hoped her family would find peace after her passing, that they would not forget the lessons of hard work and love.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He swallowed hard, his voice trembling slightly as he promised O-lan and Wang Lung that he would work diligently to ensure the marriage feast was a success, even if it meant sacrificing much.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: She squeezed Wang Lung's hand, her voice barely audible, expressing her gratitude and trust in him and their son to carry on their legacy.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He nodded again, his voice still trembling, assuring O-lan and Wang Lung that he would do his utmost to make their last wish come true.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: She squeezed Wang Lung's hand again, her eyes fixed on him and the eldest son, urging them to promise once more that they would look after each other and the family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He swallowed again, his heart heavy with the weight of his mother’s hopes and fears, and nodded solemnly at O-lan and Wang Lung, promising them with a mixture of determination and sorrow that he would fulfill their wish.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung felt a weight lift from his heart, seeing the determination in his son’s eyes, and he patted the eldest son’s shoulder, reassuring O-lan and the son that their family would thrive, no matter what.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Satisfied yet worried, O-lan looked at Wang Lung and the eldest son, her eyes filled with a mixture of relief and sorrow, urging them to ensure the family's future with every fiber of their being.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He nodded again, his heart heavy with the weight of his mother’s wishes, and looked at O-lan and Wang Lung, promising them with a mixture of determination and sorrow that he would do everything in his power to see to the family's future.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
